title: Gull Feroza, Nashra Sandhu Power Pakistan Women Past Sri Lanka in Series Opener
excerpt: Opener Gull Feroza's attacking 78 and Nashra Sandhu's three-wicket haul guided Pakistan to a comfortable five-wicket win in the first ODI at Hambantota, giving the visitors a 1-0 lead in the ICC Women's Championship series.
body:
• Gull Feroza struck 78 off 77 balls with 11 fours and was named Player of the Match as Pakistan chased down 211 with 42 balls to spare.
  • Left-arm spinner Nashra Sandhu took 3 for 42, dismissing both Sri Lankan openers and captain Chamari Athapaththu for 46.
  • Pakistan take a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series, which is part of the ICC Women's Championship 2025-29 cycle.

Pakistan Chase Down 211 With Ease

Pakistan Women began their tour of Sri Lanka with a statement, cruising to a five-wicket victory in the first ODI at the Mahinda Rajapaksa International Cricket Stadium in Hambantota on Thursday. Opener Gull Feroza smashed 78 off 77 balls, and left-arm spinner Nashra Sandhu claimed three wickets as Pakistan overhauled Sri Lanka's 210 for 9 with seven overs to spare.

The win gives Pakistan a 1-0 lead in the three-match series, which carries points for the ICC Women's Championship 2025-29. Both sides entered the contest level on four wins from six matches in the current cycle, making every game a direct battle for qualification advantage.

Sandhu and Rubab Strangle Sri Lanka's Middle Order

Sri Lanka, electing to bat first, got off to a brisk start through openers Vishmi Gunaratne and captain Chamari Athapaththu, who put on 56 for the first wicket. Gunaratne struck four boundaries in her 28 before Sandhu had her caught to break the stand in the 12th over.

Athapaththu pressed on, adding 53 for the second wicket with Hasini Perera. The captain looked set for a big score, compiling 46 off 67 balls with six fours, but Sandhu breached her defence to end a dangerous innings. It was a dismissal that shifted momentum decisively.

"Pakistan's disciplined bowling tightened the scoring through the middle overs, with Nashra Sandhu leading the attack brilliantly."

— CricketWorld match report

Perera (35) and Kavisha Dilhari (35) laboured through the middle overs against Pakistan's tight lines without ever breaking free. Sandhu finished with 3 for 42, while left-arm pacer Tasmia Rubab chipped in with 2 for 34, repeatedly breaking partnerships before they could develop. Only a late-innings flourish from Nilakshi de Silva, who hammered an unbeaten 46 off 50 deliveries, carried Sri Lanka past the 200 mark.

Feroza Takes the Game Away Early

Pakistan's chase was built on aggression from the first ball. Feroza and Sadaf Shamas raced to 58 in the opening powerplay before Shamas fell in the final over of the fielding restrictions. The early dismissal hardly mattered — Feroza was already in full flow.

Striking the ball cleanly through the off side and pulling anything short with authority, Feroza reached her half-century off just 47 deliveries. She found a willing ally in Sidra Amin, whose contrasting approach — a patient 57 off 94 balls — allowed Feroza to keep attacking without risk at both ends. The pair added 90 for the second wicket, effectively killing the contest.

Feroza departed for 78 in the 29th over, having hit 11 fours in a knock that set the template for the chase. Dilhari, Sri Lanka's best bowler on the day with 2 for 37, triggered a minor wobble — three wickets fell for 22 runs in the space of nine overs — but Pakistan were never in real trouble.

Ayesha Zafar steadied the ship with an unbeaten 27 off 31 balls and steered Pakistan across the finish line in the 43rd over.

ICC Women's Championship Context

The result carries weight beyond the bilateral series. Pakistan and Sri Lanka sit second and third respectively in the ICC Women's Championship 2025-29 standings, and points from this series feed directly into automatic qualification for the 2029 ODI World Cup. A series win for either side would significantly strengthen their position in the cycle.

Captain Fatima Sana, who led the bowling changes adeptly, will be keen to wrap up the series in the second ODI on Saturday before departing for The Hundred, where she will represent Birmingham Phoenix — becoming the first Pakistani woman to play in the competition.

What's Next

The second ODI takes place at the same venue on Saturday, July 25. A win would seal Pakistan's first ODI series victory in Sri Lanka in recent memory and pile pressure on Athapaththu's side heading into the final match on July 28. The tour then shifts to three T20Is starting July 31, with Muneeba Ali Siddiqui captaining Pakistan after Sana departs for England.
